welcome.speaker: Senator Lucius
welcome.text: Rome needs stability. I say a strong leader can act while the Senate argues. I have prepared a very impressive speech. It even has hand gestures.

welcome.speaker: Senator Cassius
welcome.text: And I say power needs limits. A dramatic hand gesture is not a system of government. New senator, choose one of our claims to challenge. Ask the question that makes us explain ourselves.

leadership.speaker: Senator Lucius
leadership.text: Who would stop a strong leader from abusing power? That is inconveniently good. My speech did not get that far. I will need evidence about leadership and accountability. Apparently the hand gestures were not enough.

limits.speaker: Senator Cassius
limits.text: How would the Senate solve a crisis if its members cannot agree? Fair challenge. Saying that power needs limits does not prove our institutions will work. I need evidence for that part of my argument too.

handoff.speaker: The Senate Clerk
handoff.text: Your seat is ready. Bring a claim, bring evidence, and be ready for someone to disagree. The laurel wreath adds exactly zero evidence. You may still wear it with confidence.
